correctness.rationale: The second variation follows from direct Taylor expansion and factors into a scalar coefficient times the variance form. Maximizing t(log t)^2 gives the exact diagonal Hessian threshold, and an exact one-coordinate factorization gives the negative critical cubic term for n>=3.

originality.rationale: The 2014 source states the all-n theorem and parameterized conjecture. A 2016 correction explicitly invalidates several neighboring statements but not these. Searches through later related literature did not locate the n>=4 counterexamples or the e^2/(2n) diagonal-instability boundary. Originality is to the best of our knowledge.

value.rationale: The result refutes a published all-n theorem for every n>=4 and gives a quantified analytic obstruction for the associated parameter conjecture, including the critical value for n>=3.

limitations: Local nonnegativity of the Hessian below the threshold does not imply the global inequality.
